rationale: Zero pixels follow coordinates modulo 3: row residue 0 maps column residues 1 and 2 to 4 and 5; row residue 1 maps column residue 1 to 6; row residue 2 maps column residue 1 to 3. Other pixels stay unchanged, as demonstrated repeatedly across different grid sizes.

Using zero-based parity, zeros become 3 at even-row odd-column positions, 4 at odd-row even-column positions, and 2 at odd-row odd-column positions. Colour 2 becomes 7 only at even-row even-column positions; the first demonstration shows all these cases.

Interior colours 1, 2, and 3 become 4, 5, and 9. Border colours 1 and 2 remain unchanged, while border colour 3 becomes 0. In the first demonstration, adjacent border and interior 3 pixels become 0 and 9 respectively.

Outputs depend on own colour and both nonzero colour sets. In demonstration 1, the changed zero has row set {1,2} and column set {1,3}, yielding 5. In demonstration 2, colour 3 with row set {2,3} and column set {1,3} becomes 7.
Row set {2,3} maps zeros to 4; row set {1,2,3} maps zeros to 7 and colour 2 to 6; row set {1,2} maps colour 1 to 8. Demonstration 6 exhibits all three row transformations.

Both row and column colour sets determine the mapping. In demonstration 2, row set {1,3} and column set {2,3} map a zero to 6 and a 3 to 5. Demonstration 7 also maps colour 2 to 4 and colour 3 to 2 under their respective combined sets.
Border zeros become 4 and interior zeros become 5. Interior colour 2 becomes 0; border colour 3 becomes 9. The first demonstration contrasts border and interior instances of each affected colour.

Zeros are filled according to the row's nonzero set: {1} gives 1, {3} gives 3, {1,3} gives 2, and {2,3} gives 1. Other row sets preserve zeros. Demonstrations 1, 4, and 9 show these mappings while preserving nonzero pixels.

Border zeros become 2, border ones become 0, and border twos become 4. Interior zeros become 3; other interior colours and all threes remain unchanged. Demonstration 1 contains each border/interior distinction.

The full 3x3 neighbourhood, including boundary padding, identifies the sparse changes. Demonstrations 1 and 7 share the all-zero in-grid neighbourhood at the top-left corner and map its centre to 2; demonstrations 1 and 3 share the bottom-edge zero neighbourhood that maps to 8.
